front.title: Security Events for Revocation of Agent Delegations

abstract.t: When a person withdraws a task from an agent, or a delegating agent is compromised, every credential delegated below that point has to stop working, and the agents holding those credentials have to stop the work they were doing under them. Token status lists and token introspection tell a verifier that asks whether one token is still valid. They do not tell the agents further down a delegation chain, which may be in other organizations and which the revoking party may not know. This document defines a Security Event Token that revokes a delegation and everything delegated from it, a subject identifier format that names a delegation token, the parties entitled to issue the event, how agents propagate it down the chain, and how verifiers check the status of a whole chain so that revocation reaches them even when the event does not.
